# QS-CFW-4919-21 - Quality specification - connecting rod CFW-4919-21 (1045)

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P2  
Parts: CFW-4919-21

Scope
This quality specification applies to the connecting rod CFW-4919-21 produced by Plant P2. It defines acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for forged, machined, and heat-treated connecting rods identified as CFW-4919-21. The scope covers dimensional, metallurgical, and mass requirements as they relate to final inspection prior to release for assembly. Use this document as the controlled reference for quality decisions and for generation of inspection records for each lot or material flow.

Requirements table
The following characteristics are required for acceptance of CFW-4919-21. Values are mandatory and must be used exactly as specified.

- Characteristic: Hardness (post heat-treat, machined bearing surfaces)  
  Requirement: The hardness range for connecting rod CFW-4919-21 (CFW-4919-21) is 29-32 HRC.

- Characteristic: Bore diameter (main bearing bores, final machined)  
  Requirement: The bore diameter tolerance for connecting rod CFW-4919-21 (CFW-4919-21) is ±0.10 mm.

- Characteristic: Forging mass (raw forging weight before trimming)  
  Requirement: The maximum forging weight for connecting rod CFW-4919-21 (CFW-4919-21) is 8.0 kg.

Notes on requirements:
- Hardness applies to the machined bearing contact surfaces and to any specified journal faces; atypical heat-treat variations must be resolved per the nonconformance handling section.
- Bore diameter tolerance is relative to the drawing nominal dimension; the tolerance value above is the allowable deviation after final machining and finish processes.
- Maximum forging weight applies to the raw forging condition; any forging exceeding the specified mass must be segregated and dispositioned.

Inspection method
General:
All inspections shall be carried out by trained inspection personnel using calibrated equipment. Calibration certificates must be traceable and available in inspection records. Visual inspection is a prerequisite before dimensional and hardness testing; parts exhibiting visible defects must be flagged and processed per nonconformance handling.

Hardness measurement:
- Measure hardness on the designated machined bearing surfaces using a Rockwell hardness tester set to the appropriate scale compatible with the requirement. Indent locations shall avoid edges, holes, and fillets and be in flat, representative surface areas.
- Record the measured values on the inspection record for each part. If a reading falls outside the specified range, perform a verification check at an adjacent location. If verification confirms out-of-specification, tag the part for nonconformance review.

Bore diameter measurement:
- Use bore gauges or internal micrometers appropriate for the bore geometry to determine the final bore diameter. Measurements shall be taken at multiple radial positions around the bore to detect out-of-round conditions and at multiple positions along the bore length to detect taper.
- Report measurements as nominal dimension plus or minus the specified tolerance. Parts with any measured value outside the tolerance shall be marked and moved to nonconformance handling.

Forging mass verification:
- Verify forging mass using calibrated industrial scales placed on a stable, level surface. Record the mass of each forging prior to trimming.
- Any forging mass recorded greater than the stated maximum shall be segregated and flagged for engineering disposition.

Sampling and records:
- Each inspected part shall have an inspection record that includes identification of the part, the inspector's initials, equipment identifiers, the measured values for hardness and bore diameter, and the forging mass. Records shall also include a brief description of any observed surface condition that could affect measurement validity.
- Maintain inspection records in the document control system under the part identifier CFW-4919-21. Inspection records are the primary evidence for acceptance and must be available for quality audits.

Examples and rationale
- Example: A connecting rod presents a hardness measurement at the bearing face of 31 HRC and a bore measurement within the handheld gauge readout that aligns with the nominal plus the stated tolerance. This part meets the hardness and bore criteria and may proceed to assembly staging.
- Example: A forging weighs 8.05 kg when placed on the calibrated scale prior to trimming. Because the mass exceeds the maximum forging weight specified, the forging is segregated and placed on hold for disposition; record the scale identifier and inspector notes.
- Rationale: Hardness band and tight bore control are critical for bearing fit and fatigue life. Forging mass control ensures the die and material usage conform to designed blanks and prevents downstream machining burden that could affect dimensional stability.

Nonconformance handling
Identification and segregation:
- Any part or forging found not to meet the requirements in the requirements table shall be immediately identified, segregated from conforming material, and marked to prevent accidental use.

Disposition:
- The quality engineer or authorized disposition authority shall review nonconforming items using available inspection data and process records. Options include rework, reheat, scrap, or return to supplier as applicable.
- Decisions shall be documented on the nonconformance record for the affected part or lot, including the reason for disposition, any rework instructions, and the identity of the approver.

Rework controls:
- Where rework is allowed to correct a nonconformance, the rework instruction must include the required verification method and acceptance criteria, which are those stated in this specification. Reworked parts must be reinspected and recorded before release.

Root cause and corrective action:
- For recurring nonconformances, perform a root cause analysis and document corrective actions. Corrective actions may include process adjustment, tool maintenance, or additional operator training. Maintain records linking corrective actions to the nonconformance events.

Records to keep
- Inspection records for each part, including hardness readings, bore dimension measurements, forging mass measurements, equipment identifiers, and inspector identification.
- Calibration certificates for measurement equipment used for hardness, bore, and mass verification.
- Nonconformance records for all parts that failed acceptance, including disposition decisions and approvals.
- Corrective action records where applicable.

This document is the controlled quality specification for CFW-4919-21 at Plant P2. Follow documented procedures and recordkeeping to ensure traceability and repeatability of inspection outcomes.
